title: Integrated Build-and-Check (Lab)
summary: Students run a full build-and-check task across four stations, record accuracy and risk verdicts, decide whether to use the output, and diagnose their weakest strand.
objectives: Run a small integrated build-and-check task end-to-end and record the checks made.
Identify which strand most needs work before the signature solution.
Evaluate the final output for accuracy and risk before deciding to use it.

body: This is your dress rehearsal. You will run a real task from start to finish - build it with a system and a prompt, then check it for accuracy and risk before deciding whether to use it. By the end you will know exactly which strand to sharpen before the signature solution.

sections.heading: I can…
items: I can run a build-and-check task through all four strands end-to-end.
I can record the accuracy and risk checks I made.
I can name which strand I most need to improve.

terms.definition: Producing an AI solution and then testing it before use.
Whether the output is correct, incorrect, or unclear.
How risky the output is and what would reduce it.
An action that reduces a risk.
The strand most likely to fail under pressure.

sections.heading: Build, then check
body: Building means choosing a suitable system and designing a clear [[prompt]] to reach a useful output.
Checking means triaging that output for accuracy and running a risk assessment before you decide to use it. Building without checking just produces confident mistakes.

sections.heading: Decide and diagnose
body: Your final call is **use**, **do not use**, or **use-with-changes** - and you must justify it with your two verdicts.
Then diagnose your [[weakest link]]: the strand where your evidence was thinnest. That is your focus before the signature solution.

sections.label: Let's try it - hands-on
sections.heading: Let's try it - hands-on
body: Run the four stations end-to-end. Build with a system and prompt, check for accuracy and risk, decide whether to use the output, and diagnose your weakest strand.
items: Name the system type and why it suits the task.
Triage the curated output for accuracy.
Run a risk assessment and choose a mitigation.
Decide use / do not use / use-with-changes and diagnose your weakest strand.

sections.heading: Think about it
items: Did your accuracy verdict or your risk verdict decide your use decision?
Which strand was your weakest link, and how will you strengthen it?

sections.heading: My reflection
items: Write your focus strand and one action to improve it before the signature solution.
Explain why building without checking is risky.

questions.prompt: Put the five steps of a build-and-check task in the order the lesson runs them, from first to last.

items.text: Triage the output for accuracy against the source
Decide use, do not use, or use-with-changes
Choose a system that suits the task and say why
Assess the risk in the output and choose a mitigation
Design a clear, specific prompt and produce the output

feedback.correct: That is build-and-check in order: you build with a system and a prompt, then check accuracy and risk, and only then decide.
feedback.incorrect: You build first and check second, and the decision comes last - it has to be made using both verdicts, so it cannot come before them.

questions.prompt: Sara's build-and-check record says: accuracy verdict - two of the three facts match the article, the third cannot be found in it; risk verdict - low, because no personal data was used. Which decision best fits her two verdicts?

options.text: Use-with-changes: take out or verify the fact she could not find, then use the rest
Use: the risk verdict is low, so the output is safe to use exactly as it is
Do not use: an output with even one unchecked detail has to be thrown away completely
Use: two facts out of three are correct, so most of the output is right

feedback.correct: Use-with-changes is a real third option: the low risk does not excuse the unchecked fact, but one unchecked fact does not waste the whole output either.
feedback.incorrect: A low risk verdict does not cancel out an accuracy problem, and one unchecked fact does not ruin everything - fix the weak part and use the rest.

questions.prompt: Match each station in the lab to the piece of evidence it should leave in your build-and-check record.

right.text: A named system type with a reason why it suits this task
The exact instruction you gave the tool, written out
A verdict of correct, incorrect or unclear with a reason you can check against the source
A named thing that could go wrong plus the mitigation you chose for it

feedback.correct: Four stations, four pieces of evidence - that record is what makes your final decision defensible.
feedback.incorrect: Each station leaves its own evidence: a justified system choice, the prompt itself, an accuracy verdict with a checkable reason, and a risk with its mitigation.

questions.prompt: Yusuf has to justify his use decision. Which of these actually support that decision, according to the lesson? Select all that apply.

options.text: His accuracy verdict, with a reason he can check against the source
His risk verdict, with the mitigation he chose
A note of which parts of the output he could not check
The output is neatly laid out and sounds confident
The tool produced the answer in under two seconds
The output is longer and more detailed than his classmates' outputs

feedback.correct: A use decision rests on the two verdicts and on being honest about what you could not check - not on how the output looks.
feedback.incorrect: Neat layout, speed and length tell you nothing about whether the output is true or safe - that is exactly how building without checking produces confident mistakes.

questions.prompt: True or false? Hamad finished the risk station faster than any other station, so that speed is good evidence that risk is his strongest strand.

feedback.correct: Right - you diagnose your strands by how thin or thick your recorded evidence is, not by how quickly you got through a station.
feedback.incorrect: Finishing fast often means thin evidence. Your weakest link is the strand where the evidence you recorded was thinnest, whatever the clock said.

formative.targets: Integrates all Term-1 Emerging outcomes end-to-end as a rehearsal for the signature solution
formative.check: Completed build-and-check record with accuracy verdict, risk verdict, use decision, and weakeststrand diagnosis
formative.successCriteria: Runs all four strands end-to-end, records both checks, makes a justified use decision, and names a weakest strand.
